title: Medvedev announces an end to the Russian military operation while advances continue
body:
According to the Civil.ge chronology of 12 August 2008, Russian aircraft continued bombing overnight and at 09:30 bombed Gori. A Russian Iskander-M missile reportedly hit Gori's central square, killing eight civilians and injuring 15, according to Civil.ge. At 12:40 Russian President Dmitry Medvedev announced that he had ordered an end to the military operation in Georgia. Civil.ge reports that Russian forces nevertheless continued to advance in eastern and western Georgia, and that Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said President Mikheil Saakashvili "must stand down".

During the afternoon Russian aircraft bombed villages in the Kaspi and Khashuri districts, a Russian attack helicopter reportedly fired on a civilian minibus on the main highway near Gori, killing nine, and Russian troops cut the highway linking eastern and western Georgia. At 16:30 Russian troops seized the Akhaldaba television and radio transmitter, killing one employee. Georgia announced it was leaving the Commonwealth of Independent States, and tens of thousands rallied in Tbilisi.

In the west, Russian-backed Abkhaz forces occupied Ganmukhuri and captured the Kodori Valley, and Russian troops destroyed Georgian military and patrol vessels in Poti. In the evening French President Nicolas Sarkozy arrived in Tbilisi from Moscow with a ceasefire draft, and amendments to the six-point agreement were made with Moscow's consent. These are the Georgian outlet's reports.
